frame.origin: centre of the heart-wall bounding box

explode_semantics: displayed position = rest position + t * (layer.explode + structure.explode), t in [0, 1], in the parent layer's space (scene units). The anterior heart half swings open along the cut-plane normal while the posterior half, valves and great vessels stay; coronary branches and cardiac veins ride on the heart half they lie on. The skin is an enclosing shell: fade it out as it peels. camera.exploded frames the fully exploded layout (t = 1).

territories.method: Soft nearest-artery assignment: softmax(-d/sigma) over the distances from each heart-wall vertex to the LAD (+septal), LCX and RCA (+marginal, PDA, posterolateral, septal) groups, sigma = 7.0 mm, faded to zero on atria and great-vessel roots (thin wall and closer to inflow/outflow vessels than to ventricular landmarks) and far from every artery; on ventricular myocardium blended 85 % towards the AHA-17 standard territories (Cerqueira 2002), the septum split between the LAD and RCA septal perforators, and the three weights re-balanced towards the population shares of LV myocardium (LAD 42.5 %, LCX 28.8 %, RCA 26.4 %).
territories.interpretation: Approximates the standard coronary perfusion territories of the AHA 17-segment model on this right-dominant BodyParts3D heart. It is a vessel-level supply map, NOT a lesion map: model outputs are per-vessel probabilities and never localise a stenosis within a vessel.

layers.label: Skin
layers.description: Thoracic skin envelope, cropped from the clavicles to below the costal margin.

layers.label: Rib cage
layers.description: Ribs, costal cartilages, sternum, clavicles and thoracic spine.

layers.label: Lungs & airway
layers.description: Five pulmonary lobes, trachea, main bronchi and the oesophagus behind them.

layers.label: Diaphragm
layers.description: Musculotendinous floor of the thoracic cavity.

layers.label: Heart
layers.description: Myocardium, epicardial fat, valves, papillary muscles, great vessels and their arch branches, and the cardiac veins.

layers.label: Coronary arteries
layers.description: Epicardial coronary tree (right-dominant) mapped to the LAD / LCX / RCA model outputs.

structures.label: Skin (thorax)
structures.description: Skin of the anterior and lateral chest wall, cropped from the clavicles to below the costal margin with the upper limbs removed.
structures.definition: Skin of the anterior and lateral thoracic wall from the clavicles to below the costal margin (epidermis surface of the BodyParts3D whole-body skin, upper limbs removed).
structures.clinical_relevance: Landmark surface for auscultation and for the surface projection of the heart: apex beat in the left 5th intercostal space at the mid-clavicular line.

structures.label: Left pectoralis major
structures.description: Clavicular and sternocostal parts of the left pectoralis major, the large fan-shaped muscle overlying the anterior chest wall.
structures.definition: Left pectoralis major: clavicular head (medial half of the clavicle) and sternocostal head (sternum and costal cartilages 1-6), converging on the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus (cut at the shoulder plane).
structures.clinical_relevance: Overlies the anterior heart border; the window for parasternal echocardiography and the plane for device pockets lies beneath it.

structures.label: Right pectoralis major
structures.description: Clavicular and sternocostal parts of the right pectoralis major.
structures.definition: Right pectoralis major: clavicular and sternocostal heads converging on the humerus (cut at the shoulder plane).
structures.clinical_relevance: Overlies the right atrium and superior vena cava; site of the right infraclavicular venous access route.

structures.label: Left ribs (1–12)
structures.description: Left ribs 1–12: true ribs 1–7 articulate with the sternum through their costal cartilages, false ribs 8–10 join the costal margin and floating ribs 11–12 end free.
structures.definition: Left ribs 1-12 (bony parts; the costal cartilages are a separate node).
structures.clinical_relevance: Ribs 2-6 frame the cardiac silhouette; intercostal spaces are the reference for the apex (left 5th space) and valve projections.

structures.label: Right ribs (1–12)
structures.description: Right ribs 1–12 forming the right half of the bony thoracic cage.
structures.definition: Right ribs 1-12 (bony parts).
structures.clinical_relevance: The right heart border (right atrium) projects between the right 3rd and 6th costal cartilages.

structures.label: Costal cartilages
structures.description: Hyaline costal cartilages: the individual cartilages of ribs 1–7 forming the sternocostal joints, and the fused cartilages of ribs 8–10 that form the costal margin.
structures.definition: Hyaline costal cartilages of ribs 1-7 and the fused costal margin of ribs 8-10, joining the ribs to the sternum.
structures.clinical_relevance: Surface landmarks of the heart: superior border from left CC2 to right CC3, right border CC3-CC6, pulmonary valve at the left CC3 junction.

structures.label: Sternum
structures.description: Manubrium, body and xiphoid process of the sternum; the heart lies directly behind its lower half.
structures.definition: Manubrium, body and xiphoid process; the sternal angle (manubriosternal joint) lies at the level of the 2nd costal cartilage and the T4/T5 disc.
structures.clinical_relevance: Median sternotomy is the standard access for cardiac surgery; the sternal angle marks the start and end of the aortic arch and the carina.

structures.label: Left clavicle
structures.description: Left collarbone, strut between the sternum and the shoulder.
structures.definition: Left clavicle, from the sternoclavicular to the acromioclavicular joint.
structures.clinical_relevance: Landmark for the left subclavian vein (device leads) and the mid-clavicular line used to locate the apex beat.

structures.label: Right clavicle
structures.description: Right collarbone, strut between the sternum and the shoulder.
structures.definition: Right clavicle, from the sternoclavicular to the acromioclavicular joint.
structures.clinical_relevance: Landmark for subclavian and internal jugular venous access; the right brachiocephalic vein forms behind its sternal end.

structures.label: Thoracic spine (T1–T12)
structures.description: Twelve thoracic vertebrae forming the posterior wall of the thorax; the descending aorta runs along their left anterior surface.
structures.definition: Thoracic vertebrae T1-T12.
structures.clinical_relevance: Vertebral levels locate the carina (T4/T5), pulmonary-artery bifurcation (T5-T6) and IVC hiatus (T8); the descending aorta lies left anterolateral to the bodies.

structures.label: Left lung
structures.description: Left lung (upper and lower lobes). Its cardiac notch accommodates the heart, which is why most of the heart lies left of the midline.
structures.definition: Left lung: superior lobe (with the lingula) and inferior lobe; the cardiac notch of the superior lobe leaves a bare area of pericardium at the 5th intercostal space.
structures.clinical_relevance: The cardiac notch is the acoustic window for apical echocardiography; lung tissue overlying the heart limits transthoracic imaging.

structures.label: Right lung
structures.description: Right lung (upper, middle and lower lobes).
structures.definition: Right lung: superior, middle and inferior lobes; its mediastinal surface is grooved by the right atrium, superior vena cava and azygos vein.
structures.clinical_relevance: The middle lobe abuts the right heart border; right pulmonary veins drain into the left atrium behind the right atrium and SVC.

structures.label: Trachea & bronchi
structures.description: Trachea and bronchial tree; the tracheal bifurcation (carina) lies just above and behind the left atrium.
structures.definition: Trachea and bronchial tree; the carina (tracheal bifurcation) lies at T4/T5, the left main bronchus passes under the aortic arch.
structures.clinical_relevance: A widened subcarinal angle is a radiographic sign of left-atrial enlargement; the left atrium lies directly below the carina.

structures.label: Oesophagus
structures.description: Muscular tube of the posterior mediastinum, behind the trachea and directly behind the left atrium below about T5; the descending aorta lies to its left and, near the diaphragm, behind it.
structures.definition: Thoracic oesophagus in the posterior mediastinum: behind the trachea, then directly behind the left atrium below about T5 (the oesophagus is in contact with the posterior left-atrial wall over a length of 58 +/- 14 mm on CT), with the descending aorta to its left and, near the diaphragm, behind it.
structures.clinical_relevance: The window for transoesophageal echocardiography; at risk of atrio-oesophageal fistula during left-atrial (pulmonary-vein) ablation.

structures.label: Diaphragm
structures.description: Dome-shaped respiratory muscle; the inferior (diaphragmatic) wall of the heart rests on its central tendon.
structures.definition: Musculotendinous floor of the thorax; the heart rests on its central tendon, fused to the fibrous pericardium; the IVC passes through it at T8.
structures.clinical_relevance: The inferior (diaphragmatic) wall of the heart, supplied by the PDA, lies on it; inferior myocardial infarction can mimic abdominal pain.

structures.label: Myocardium (anterior half)
structures.description: Anterior half of the heart wall (epicardial and endocardial surfaces), opened along the long axis. Vertex colours carry approximate LAD / LCX / RCA perfusion-territory weights (AHA 17-segment convention) — not a lesion map.
structures.provenance: BodyParts3D, with three documented local corrections (synthesis stage): the wall yields round the moved aortic root, the posterolateral left atrium is stretched so the left pulmonary veins enter 25-37 mm from the mitral hinge, and the right-atrial roof round the SVC is lowered 10 mm; channels are carved for the vessels that pass under the fused tip of the left auricle
structures.definition: Anterior half of the heart wall (myocardium of all four chambers), opened by a long-axis cut through both ventricles; carries the sternocostal surface: right ventricle, anterior interventricular groove and the anterior left ventricle.
structures.clinical_relevance: Its COLOR_0 weights are the LAD / LCX / RCA perfusion territories used to colour model risk (a supply map, never a lesion map).

structures.label: Myocardium (posterior half)
structures.description: Posterior half of the heart wall including the inferior (diaphragmatic) surface and the atria. Vertex colours carry approximate perfusion-territory weights — not a lesion map.
structures.provenance: BodyParts3D, with three documented local corrections (synthesis stage): the wall yields round the moved aortic root, the posterolateral left atrium is stretched so the left pulmonary veins enter 25-37 mm from the mitral hinge, and the right-atrial roof round the SVC is lowered 10 mm; channels are carved for the vessels that pass under the fused tip of the left auricle
structures.definition: Posterior half of the heart wall, opened by the same long-axis cut: left atrium, lateral and inferior (diaphragmatic) left-ventricular walls, posterior interventricular groove and crux.
structures.clinical_relevance: Inferior and inferolateral walls (AHA segments 3-5, 9-11, 15) are RCA / LCX territory in a right-dominant heart.

structures.label: Mitral valve
structures.description: Bicuspid valve between the left atrium and left ventricle: the anterior (aortic) leaflet, in fibrous continuity with the aortic root, and the scalloped posterior leaflet, tethered by chordae tendineae to the anterolateral and posteromedial papillary muscles (designed on the BodyParts3D hinge and papillary muscles).
structures.provenance: Synthesised on the BodyParts3D annulus and papillary muscles (anatomy/scripts/valves.py)
structures.definition: Left atrioventricular valve, shown half open: the anterior (aortic) leaflet, about 22 mm tall on the third of the annulus next to the aortic root and in fibrous continuity with it, and the posterior leaflet, about 12.5 mm tall with three scallops (P1-P3), both thin veils thickening at the rough zone; first- and second-order chordae tendineae fan from the two heads of the anterolateral and posteromedial papillary muscles to the free edges and rough zones of both leaflets.
structures.clinical_relevance: Mitral regurgitation after inferior or lateral infarction follows papillary-muscle dysfunction (posteromedial muscle: single RCA/PDA supply).

structures.label: Tricuspid valve
structures.description: Three-leaflet valve between the right atrium and right ventricle (anterior, septal and posterior leaflets); the septal leaflet is hinged on the septum a little more apically than the anterior mitral leaflet.
structures.provenance: Synthesised on the BodyParts3D annulus and papillary muscles (anatomy/scripts/valves.py)
structures.definition: Right atrioventricular valve with anterior (largest), septal and posterior leaflets, shown half open, tethered by chordae to the anterior, posterior and septal papillary muscles; the septal leaflet is hinged on the septum 7 mm more apically than the anterior mitral hinge (normal apical offset 5-10 mm; > 8 mm/m2 suggests Ebstein anomaly).
structures.clinical_relevance: The RCA runs in the right AV groove next to its annulus (injury risk in tricuspid annuloplasty); apical displacement of the septal leaflet > 8 mm/m2 indicates Ebstein anomaly.

structures.label: Pulmonary valve
structures.description: Semilunar valve at the right-ventricular outflow into the pulmonary trunk.
structures.definition: Semilunar valve at the right-ventricular outflow (conus), anterior, superior and to the left of the aortic valve; projects at the junction of the sternum and left 3rd costal cartilage.
structures.clinical_relevance: The pulmonary trunk and left main coronary artery are neighbours: the LM runs behind the trunk.

structures.label: Aortic valve
structures.description: Tricuspid semilunar valve at the left-ventricular outflow: right, left and non-coronary cusps hinged in the sinuses of Valsalva (synthesised; BodyParts3D has no aortic valve).
structures.definition: Aortic valve: three semilunar cusps (right, left, non-coronary) hinged in a crown-shaped line in the sinuses of Valsalva from the annulus to the sino-tubular junction, each with a thin lunula and a nodule of Arantius at the centre of its free edge; the right and left sinuses give the RCA and left-main ostia. The annulus is in fibrous continuity with the anterior mitral leaflet (aorto-mitral curtain). Geometry synthesised (BodyParts3D has no aortic valve).
structures.clinical_relevance: Coronary ostial height above the annulus (MDCT ~14 mm LM, ~17 mm RCA) governs coronary-obstruction risk in transcatheter aortic valve implantation.

structures.label: Papillary muscles
structures.description: Right- and left-ventricular papillary muscles. The posteromedial LV papillary muscle usually has a single blood supply (RCA/PDA), which makes it vulnerable in inferior infarction.
structures.provenance: Synthesised cones placed from the BodyParts3D papillary muscles (anatomy/scripts/valves.py)
structures.definition: Papillary muscles: the left-ventricular anterolateral and posteromedial muscles (each with two heads) and the right-ventricular anterior, posterior and septal muscles, rising from the ventricular wall and anchoring the chordae tendineae of the atrioventricular valves.
structures.clinical_relevance: The posteromedial LV papillary muscle has a single (usually RCA/PDA) supply and is the one that ruptures after inferior infarction.

structures.label: Aorta
structures.description: Aortic root with the three sinuses of Valsalva (right / left / non-coronary, synthesised), ascending aorta, arch and descending thoracic aorta. The right sinus gives the right coronary artery and the left sinus the left main.
structures.provenance: BodyParts3D arch / descending aorta; ascending calibre corrected; root synthesised and placed at the anterior mitral hinge
structures.definition: Aortic root (annulus, three sinuses of Valsalva, sino-tubular junction; synthesised), ascending aorta (calibre corrected to an in-vivo value), arch (T4, over the right pulmonary artery and left main bronchus) and descending thoracic aorta (left of the spine, behind the left atrium and oesophagus).
structures.clinical_relevance: Both coronary arteries arise from its root; ascending-aortic dilatation (> 41 mm) and root anatomy matter for aortic surgery and TAVI.

structures.label: Aortic arch branches
structures.description: Brachiocephalic trunk (dividing into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries), left common carotid and left subclavian arteries, from right to left along the arch.
structures.definition: Branches of the aortic arch from right to left: brachiocephalic trunk (dividing into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries), left common carotid and left subclavian arteries (standard three-branch arch, ~75-81 %).
structures.clinical_relevance: Arch anatomy determines catheter access for coronary angiography from the radial or femoral route and the risk of stroke in arch interventions.

structures.label: Pulmonary artery
structures.description: Pulmonary trunk, its right and left branches and the intrapulmonary arterial tree, carrying deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs.
structures.definition: Pulmonary trunk from the RV outflow (in front of and then left of the ascending aorta), bifurcating at T5-T6 into the right pulmonary artery (behind the ascending aorta and SVC) and the left pulmonary artery (over the left main bronchus), with the intrapulmonary branches.
structures.clinical_relevance: A main pulmonary artery wider than the ascending aorta (ratio > 1) suggests pulmonary hypertension. Vertex attributes _DIST_HEART / _DIST_HILUM separate the proximal trunk from the intrapulmonary tree.

structures.label: Pulmonary veins
structures.description: Pulmonary veins and their intrapulmonary tributaries, returning oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.
structures.provenance: BodyParts3D; the left veins moved with the stretched posterolateral left atrium (synthesised: SYN_PulmonaryVeins)
structures.definition: Pulmonary veins (two right and two left) entering the smooth posterior-superior wall of the left atrium, with their intrapulmonary tributaries; the left ostia lie 25-32 mm from the mitral hinge (the mitral isthmus; in vivo 20-40 mm).
structures.clinical_relevance: Pulmonary-vein isolation (ablation of atrial fibrillation) targets their left-atrial ostia; _DIST_HEART / _DIST_HILUM give the distance from those ostia and from the lung hilum.

structures.label: Superior vena cava
structures.description: Superior vena cava draining the upper body into the right atrium.
structures.provenance: BodyParts3D, lengthened with the lowered right-atrial roof (synthesised: SYN_SVC)
structures.definition: Superior vena cava, formed behind the right 1st costal cartilage by the brachiocephalic veins, running vertically to the right of the ascending aorta into the roof of the right atrium at the level of the right 3rd costal cartilage; 45 mm long in this model (in vivo 60-80 mm: BodyParts3D's is short).
structures.clinical_relevance: Route of central venous catheters and pacemaker leads; the sino-atrial node lies at its junction with the right atrium.

structures.label: Brachiocephalic veins
structures.description: Right and left brachiocephalic veins, each formed behind the sternoclavicular joint by the internal jugular and subclavian veins; they join behind the right first costal cartilage to form the superior vena cava. The left vein crosses in front of the arch branches.
structures.definition: Right and left brachiocephalic veins, each formed behind the sternoclavicular joint by the internal jugular and subclavian veins (stubs shown); the longer left vein crosses in front of the arch branches to join the right behind the right 1st costal cartilage.
structures.clinical_relevance: Venous access route for central lines and transvenous pacing leads; the left vein can be compressed by an elongated aortic arch.

structures.label: Inferior vena cava
structures.description: Terminal thoracic segment of the inferior vena cava entering the right atrium through the diaphragm.
structures.definition: Inferior vena cava: passes the central tendon of the diaphragm at T8 and enters the posteroinferior right atrium after a short thoracic course (diameter < 21 mm).
structures.clinical_relevance: IVC calibre and collapsibility estimate right-atrial pressure on echocardiography; the coronary-sinus ostium lies in front of and medial to its orifice.

structures.label: Cardiac veins
structures.description: Coronary venous tree draining through the coronary sinus into the right atrium: coronary sinus, great cardiac vein and anterior interventricular vein (beside the LAD and LCX), middle cardiac vein (with the PDA), posterior veins of the left ventricle, plus the anterior cardiac veins that cross the RCA and open directly into the right atrium.
structures.provenance: Designed on this heart around the corrected coronary tree (anatomy/scripts/veins.py): BodyParts3D courses where they agree, in-vivo calibres, one lumen
structures.definition: Coronary venous tree: the coronary sinus (48 mm) in the posterior left AV groove on the atrial side of the mitral annulus, opening flush into the posteroinferior right atrium in front of the IVC orifice; the great cardiac vein (110 mm) in the left AV groove on the atrial side of the LCX, below the left auricle, turning at the left-main bifurcation into the anterior interventricular vein (115 mm) beside the LAD; the middle cardiac vein with the PDA, joining the sinus 14 mm from its ostium; the posterior vein of the LV and the left marginal vein; the small cardiac vein (63 mm) in the posterior right AV groove beside the RCA, receiving the right marginal vein from the acute margin; and 2 short anterior cardiac veins that cross the RCA and open directly into the right atrium. Per-vertex _VEIN labels (manifest veins[]).
structures.clinical_relevance: The coronary sinus and its tributaries are the route for left-ventricular leads in cardiac resynchronisation therapy and for retrograde cardioplegia; the LCX runs between the coronary sinus and the mitral annulus in ~70 % (percutaneous annuloplasty risk).

structures.label: Epicardial fat (anterior half)
structures.description: Epicardial adipose tissue filling the atrioventricular and interventricular grooves around the coronary trunks and veins (synthesised).
structures.definition: Epicardial adipose tissue of the anterior half: the fat bed of the right atrioventricular groove and the anterior interventricular groove (up to ~8 mm, feathering out over 6-9 mm), lobulated, along the proximal course of the diagonal and acute marginal branches, thinning to a film over the apex; its surface lies 0.35 of a vessel radius above each groove vessel's axis, so about two-thirds of each trunk is embedded and its crown runs as a continuous ridge. Synthesised from the vessel courses (BodyParts3D has no epicardial fat).
structures.clinical_relevance: Epicardial and pericoronary fat is metabolically active; CT pericoronary fat attenuation around the proximal RCA, LAD and LCX is a marker of coronary inflammation and risk.

structures.label: Epicardial fat (posterior half)
structures.description: Epicardial adipose tissue filling the atrioventricular and interventricular grooves around the coronary trunks and veins (synthesised).
structures.definition: Epicardial adipose tissue of the posterior half: the fat bed of the posterior atrioventricular groove (coronary sinus, circumflex, distal RCA) and the posterior interventricular groove (PDA, middle cardiac vein), lobulated, feathering out over 6-9 mm; about two-thirds of each groove vessel is embedded. Synthesised from the vessel courses.
structures.clinical_relevance: Surrounds the coronary sinus and circumflex artery; excess epicardial fat is associated with atrial fibrillation and coronary artery disease.

structures.label: Left main coronary artery
structures.description: Short left main stem arising from the left aortic sinus and bifurcating into the LAD and LCX. The dataset has no separate left-main label, so this segment is not colour-coded by the model.
structures.territory: Entire LAD and LCX territories (via its two branches)
structures.provenance: Derived from BodyParts3D (re-routed from the moved left sinus to the start of the left AV groove)
structures.definition: Left main coronary artery (SCCT 5): from its ostium in the left sinus of Valsalva, leftward behind the pulmonary trunk to its bifurcation into the LAD and LCX at the anterior end of the left AV groove, under the left auricle (about 16 mm long in this model; in vivo 10 +/- 5 mm, 3.5-4.5 mm wide).
structures.clinical_relevance: Feeds both the LAD and LCX territories (~70 % of the LV); significant left-main disease is a surgical indication. Not a model target itself.

structures.label: Left anterior descending (LAD)
structures.description: Runs in the anterior interventricular groove to the apex, giving diagonal branches to the anterolateral wall and septal perforators to the septum.
structures.territory: Anterior wall, anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum and the apex (AHA segments 1, 2, 7, 8, 13, 14, 17)
structures.provenance: BodyParts3D course with a new origin at the moved left-main bifurcation; the first diagonal re-attached more proximally, RV branches trimmed, D2 and a left conus branch synthesised
structures.definition: Left anterior descending artery in the anterior interventricular groove from the LM bifurcation to (and around) the apex: SCCT 6 pLAD (to the first septal perforator or D1, whichever is first), 7 mLAD (to half-way to the apex), 8 dLAD, 9 D1 and 10 D2 (diagonals leaving it at 40-55 deg over the anterolateral LV), short right-ventricular branches and a small left conus branch over the infundibulum (the LAD half of the ring of Vieussens).
structures.clinical_relevance: Supplies the anterior wall, anterior two-thirds of the septum and the apex (AHA 1, 2, 7, 8, 13, 14, 17; ~42 % of the LV); proximal LAD occlusion causes the largest infarcts.

structures.label: LAD septal perforators
structures.description: Septal perforating branches of the LAD penetrating the interventricular septum.
structures.territory: Anterior two-thirds of the interventricular septum
structures.provenance: Synthesised (4 perforators grown into the septum; BodyParts3D perforators left the LAD backwards)
structures.definition: Septal perforating branches of the LAD leaving it at about 70 degrees and running inferoposteriorly through the interventricular septum (S1 25-40 mm, 1.5-2 mm wide; unnumbered in SCCT; labelled S1 ... S4 from proximal).
structures.clinical_relevance: Supply the anterior two-thirds of the septum and the conduction system (bundle branches); the first septal is the target of alcohol septal ablation.

structures.label: Left circumflex (LCX)
structures.description: Runs in the left atrioventricular groove around the left border of the heart, giving obtuse marginal branches to the lateral wall.
structures.territory: Lateral (anterolateral and inferolateral) wall of the left ventricle (AHA segments 5, 6, 11, 12, 16)
structures.provenance: Derived from BodyParts3D (trunk re-routed into the left AV groove; OM1 BodyParts3D; OM2 synthesised)
structures.definition: Left circumflex artery from the left-main bifurcation in the left atrioventricular groove, between the left atrium / great cardiac vein and the mitral annulus (SCCT 11 pCx to the origin of OM1, 13 LCx beyond it), round the obtuse margin; it ends on the posterolateral wall before the crux (right dominance). Obtuse marginals OM1 (SCCT 12) and OM2 (14) run towards the apex over the lateral LV wall.
structures.clinical_relevance: Supplies the lateral and inferolateral LV (AHA 5, 6, 11, 12, 16; ~29 % of the LV) and the left atrium; circumflex occlusions are often ECG-silent.

structures.label: Right coronary artery (RCA)
structures.description: Arises from the right aortic sinus and runs in the right atrioventricular groove to the crux of the heart; supplies the right ventricle, the SA and AV nodes (in most people) and, in right-dominant hearts, the inferior wall.
structures.territory: Right ventricle, inferior wall and inferior septum (AHA segments 3, 4, 9, 10, 15)
structures.provenance: Derived from BodyParts3D (re-routed into the right AV groove)
structures.definition: Right coronary artery from the right sinus of Valsalva, forward between the right auricle and pulmonary trunk, down the right atrioventricular groove (5-12 mm outside the tricuspid hinge), around the acute margin and along the inferior AV groove to the crux: SCCT 1 pRCA, 2 mRCA (to the acute margin), 3 dRCA (to the PDA origin), 16 R-PLB beyond the crux. Its first branch, the conus branch, leaves where the proximal RCA reaches the front of the heart and crosses the anterior infundibulum ~11 mm below the pulmonary valve towards the LAD's conus branch; then the sinoatrial-nodal artery.
structures.clinical_relevance: Dominant in ~85 %: supplies the right ventricle, inferior wall and inferior septum (AHA 3, 4, 9, 10, 15) and usually the SA and AV nodes (bradyarrhythmia in inferior infarction).

structures.label: Acute marginal branch (RCA)
structures.description: Right (acute) marginal branch of the RCA running along the acute margin of the right ventricle.
structures.provenance: BodyParts3D courses, re-attached to the RCA in the AV groove
structures.definition: Acute marginal and right-ventricular branches of the RCA running over the right-ventricular free wall towards the apex (unnumbered in SCCT).
structures.clinical_relevance: Supply the RV free wall; proximal RCA occlusion above them causes right-ventricular infarction.

structures.label: Posterior descending artery (PDA)
structures.description: Posterior interventricular branch; arises from the RCA in this right-dominant anatomy and runs in the posterior interventricular groove.
structures.territory: Inferior wall and inferior third of the septum (AHA segments 3, 4, 9, 10, 15)
structures.definition: Posterior descending artery (SCCT 4 R-PDA) from the RCA at the crux, running in the posterior (inferior) interventricular groove towards the apex and giving inferior septal branches.
structures.clinical_relevance: Defines right dominance; supplies the inferior wall, inferior third of the septum and the posteromedial papillary muscle.

structures.label: Posterolateral branch (RCA)
structures.description: Right posterolateral branch continuing beyond the crux onto the inferolateral left ventricle.
structures.territory: Inferior / inferolateral base of the left ventricle
structures.definition: Posterolateral branch of the RCA (SCCT 16 R-PLB) continuing beyond the crux in the left AV groove and onto the inferolateral LV base.
structures.clinical_relevance: Supplies the inferior and inferolateral LV base in right-dominant hearts, overlapping with the LCX territory.

structures.label: RCA septal branches
structures.description: Inferior septal branches arising from the PDA / RCA.
structures.territory: Inferior third of the interventricular septum
structures.provenance: Synthesised (3 short inferior septal branches grown from the PDA)
structures.definition: Inferior septal branches from the PDA (and RCA) into the posterior third of the interventricular septum (short, <= 15 mm; unnumbered in SCCT).
structures.clinical_relevance: Supply the inferior septum and often the AV node region together with the AV-nodal artery.

segments.name: Proximal RCA
segments.definition: From the RCA ostium to one-half the distance to the acute margin of the heart.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Mid RCA
segments.definition: From the end of the proximal RCA to the acute margin of the heart.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Distal RCA
segments.definition: From the end of the mid RCA (acute margin) to the origin of the posterior descending artery (crux).
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Posterior descending artery (from RCA)
segments.definition: Branch of the RCA running in the posterior (inferior) interventricular groove from the crux towards the apex.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Left main
segments.definition: From the left-main ostium in the left sinus of Valsalva to its bifurcation into the LAD and LCX.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Proximal LAD
segments.definition: From the end of the left main to the first large septal perforator or first diagonal (> 1.5 mm), whichever is most proximal.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Mid LAD
segments.definition: From the end of the proximal LAD to one-half the distance to the apex.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Distal LAD
segments.definition: From the end of the mid LAD to the end of the LAD (including its wrap around the apex).
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: First diagonal
segments.definition: First diagonal branch of the LAD, running over the anterolateral left-ventricular wall.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Second diagonal
segments.definition: Second diagonal branch of the LAD.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Proximal circumflex
segments.definition: From the end of the left main to the origin of the first obtuse marginal, in the left atrioventricular groove.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: First obtuse marginal
segments.definition: First obtuse-marginal branch of the LCX, running towards the apex over the lateral left-ventricular wall.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Mid / distal circumflex
segments.definition: Circumflex beyond the first obtuse marginal in the atrioventricular groove, to the end of the vessel or the origin of the L-PDA.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Second obtuse marginal
segments.definition: Second obtuse-marginal branch of the LCX.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Posterior descending artery (from LCX)
segments.definition: PDA arising from the LCX in left-dominant hearts (not present in this right-dominant model).
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Posterolateral branch (from RCA)
segments.definition: Posterolateral branch(es) of the RCA beyond the crux, supplying the inferior and inferolateral left-ventricular base.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Ramus intermedius
segments.definition: Branch arising from the left main between the LAD and LCX (trifurcation); absent in this model.
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

segments.name: Posterolateral branch (from LCX)
segments.definition: Posterolateral branch arising from the LCX in left-dominant hearts (not present in this model).
segments.source: SCCT 2014 (Leipsic et al., J Cardiovasc Comput Tomogr 2014;8:342-358), adapted from AHA 1975

veins.label: CS
veins.name: Coronary sinus
veins.definition: Last 48 mm of the venous tree in the posterior left AV groove, on the atrial side of the mitral annulus, from the valve of Vieussens / vein of Marshall to its ostium, which opens flush into the posteroinferior right atrium in front of and medial to the IVC orifice; about 9-10 mm wide.

veins.label: GCV
veins.name: Great cardiac vein
veins.definition: Great cardiac vein (110 mm): from the coronary sinus along the left AV groove, on the atrial side of the circumflex and never more than ~15 mm from the mitral hinge, below the left auricle to the left-main bifurcation, where it turns into the anterior interventricular vein (triangle of Brocq and Mouchet with the proximal LAD and LCX).

veins.label: AIV
veins.name: Anterior interventricular vein
veins.definition: Anterior interventricular vein (115 mm): ascends in the anterior interventricular groove beside the LAD, mostly on its left-ventricular side, from near the apex to the left-main bifurcation, where it continues as the great cardiac vein.

veins.label: MCV
veins.name: Middle cardiac vein
veins.definition: Middle cardiac vein: runs from the apex in the posterior interventricular groove with the PDA and joins the coronary sinus 14 mm from its ostium, where the sinus passes the crux.

veins.label: PVLV
veins.name: Posterior vein of the left ventricle
veins.definition: Posterior (inferolateral) left-ventricular vein between the middle cardiac and left marginal veins; in this model it drains into the great cardiac vein 62 mm from the coronary-sinus ostium.

veins.label: ACV
veins.name: Anterior cardiac veins
veins.definition: Small veins of the anterior right-ventricular wall (2 in this model, <= 45 mm) that cross the right AV groove over the RCA and open directly into the right atrium above the tricuspid annulus, bypassing the coronary sinus.

veins.label: LMV
veins.name: Left marginal vein
veins.definition: Ascends over the lateral (obtuse) margin of the left ventricle with the first obtuse marginal branch and drains into the great cardiac vein in the left AV groove (present in about two-thirds of hearts).

veins.label: SCV
veins.name: Small cardiac vein
veins.definition: Small cardiac vein (63 mm): runs in the posterior right AV groove beside the distal RCA, on its atrial side, from the acute margin (where it receives the right marginal vein) to the coronary sinus beside its ostium (present in ~40 %; designed on this heart, BodyParts3D has no mesh for it).

veins.label: RMV
veins.name: Right marginal vein
veins.definition: Right marginal vein (74 mm): ascends along the acute margin of the right ventricle with the acute marginal artery and drains into the small cardiac vein in the right AV groove.

COLOR_0.meaning: perfusion-territory weights r = LAD, g = LCX, b = RCA; 1 - (r + g + b) = neutral (atria, roots)

TEXCOORD_0.meaning: UVs of the baked PBR textures (baseColor, normal, occlusion + roughness)

_ARCLEN.meaning: normalised arc length 0 -> 1 from the ostium of the tree (left tree from the LM ostium, right tree from the RCA ostium)

_SEGMENT.meaning: SCCT 2014 segment number of the nearest labelled centreline point (1-18; 0 = named but unnumbered branch). See segments[]. Anatomical label only - never a lesion location.

_VEIN.meaning: cardiac-vein code of the nearest labelled vein centreline point, see veins[] (1 CS, 2 GCV, 3 AIV, 4 MCV, 5 PVLV, 6 ACV, 7 LMV, 8 SCV, 9 RMV; 7-8 added in v1.1, 9 in round 3)

_RADIUS.meaning: lumen radius of the nearest labelled centreline point (vessels.json radius): inflate a vessel in proportion to its calibre (e.g. r' = max(1.15 r, minimum pixel width)) and fade sub-pixel tips instead of adding a fixed offset

_TERRITORY.meaning: copy of the COLOR_0 perfusion-territory weights (r = LAD, g = LCX, b = RCA) under a custom name. Read this one: glTF viewers multiply COLOR_0 into the base colour, so a later contract version will set COLOR_0 to white.

_DIST_HEART.meaning: geodesic distance along the vessel wall from its cardiac end (pulmonary valve / left-atrial ostium)

_DIST_HILUM.meaning: signed geodesic distance from where the vessel enters a lung: < 0 outside the lungs (towards the heart), > 0 intrapulmonary. Keep dist_hilum < ~0.02 to show only the proximal (extrapulmonary) vessels.
